correctness.rationale: PASS: The standard k-PIR distance bound forces any binary linear length-17 6-PIR code on s=8 bits to have d>=6. Published classification of binary [17,8,6] codes gives one equivalence class (representable by cyclic g(x)=1+x+x³+x⁶+x⁸+x⁹). Independently enumerate its 256 primal words (d=6) and 512 dual words (dual d=5, exactly 34 weight-5 words). Across 136 coordinate pairs, 68 lie in two and 68 lie in three weight-5 dual supports, so no pair lies in five. Six pairwise disjoint nonempty recovery sets for a fixed nonzero information syndrome would have pairwise unions of size >=5 and total size <=17, forcing sorted cardinalities (2,3,3,3,3,3). The five unions of the size-2 set with each size-3 set are distinct dual weight-5 supports through a fixed pair, impossible. Therefore length17 excluded, while Kurz–Yaakobi already construct length18, proving P(8,6)=18. Source literature class uniqueness and upper bound are explicitly external premises; finite enumeration certifies the representative obstruction, not all code isomorphism classes.

evidence: PIR distance bound and published upper bound provide 17<=P(8,6)<=18. The 2025 classification is an exhaustive coding-theoretic equivalence result without an all-information-symbol recovery guarantee.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A code classification with no recovery-set condition is insufficient to imply exclusion; no broader PIR converse found that automatically excludes 17 under this exact parameter set.
